'''Leo Waldemar Törnqvist''' (14 February 1911 – 18 April 1983) was one of the first professors of statistics in Finland, and the first to achieve international recognition. He taught at the [[University of Helsinki]] from 1943 to 1974, and developed techniques that are used in official price and productivity statistics.<ref name=uf>[https://www.uppslagsverket.fi/sv/sok/view-103684-ToernqvistLeo Törnqvist, Leo] in ''[[Uppslagsverket Finland]]'' {{in lang|sv}}.</ref><ref name=sk>[http://biografiasampo.fi/henkilo/p5753 Törnqvist, Leo (1911–1983)], ''[[Suomen kansallisbiografia]]'' (in Finnish)</ref>

==Life, education, and career==
Törnqvist was born on 14 February 1911 in [[Jeppo (village)|Jeppo]], a Swedish-speaking village in Finland. He studied mathematics, physics, and chemistry at [[Åbo Akademi University]] in [[Turku]], where his interests shifted to economics and statistics under the influence of Swedish economist Arthur Montgomery. He finished his studies in Turku in 1933 and continued with graduate work in mathematics at [[Stockholm University]], earning a doctorate in 1937 under the supervision of [[Harald Cramér]] and [[Gunnar Myrdal]].<ref name=sk/>

After a short-term teaching position at [[Åbo Akademi University]] from 1937 to 1938, he began his career working for the Finnish railway service from 1938 until 1943. He was appointed as an associate professor of statistics at the University of Helsinki in 1943 and promoted to full professor in 1950. In the early 1950s he visited researchers in the US and, in the early 1960s, worked as a consultant for the United Nations in Indonesia.<ref name=sk/>

He died on 18 April 1983.<ref name=sk/>

==Contributions==
Törnqvist developed an approach to creating weighted [[price index]]es across discrete time periods using weighted averages of growth rates in prices where the weights were quantity averages across the two periods, in work he did with the [[Bank of Finland]] published in 1936.<ref>Törnqvist, Leo. 1936. The Bank of Finland's Consumption Price Index. ''Bank of Finland Monthly Bulletin'' 10, 1–8.</ref><ref>Törnqvist, Leo. 1981. ''Collected scientific papers of Leo Tornqvist.'' Research Institute of the Finnish Economy. Series A. {{ISBN|951-9205-74-8}}</ref> These [[Törnqvist index]]es are used in official price and productivity statistics in many countries.<ref>''"BLS aggregates inputs for its multifactor productivity measures using a Tornqvist chain index."'' U.S. [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]]. 1997. [https://www.bls.gov/opub/hom/pdf/msp-19970714.pdf Chapter 10. Productivity Measures: Business Sector and Major Subsectors]. ''BLS Handbook of Methods''. 1997.</ref><ref>''"The Tornqvist index is used in the calculation of multifactor productivity."'' [http://www.pc.gov.au/research/productivity/estimates-trends/methodology Methodology] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928000903/http://www.pc.gov.au/research/productivity/estimates-trends/methodology |date=28 September 2011 }} Australian Government [[Productivity Commission]], 2009. Viewed 11 August 2011.</ref><ref>[http://www.ers.usda.gov/publications/tb1872/tb1872d.pdf The Tornqvist Index as a True-Cost Index] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100615153935/http://www.ers.usda.gov/publications/tb1872/tb1872d.pdf |date=15 June 2010 }}, in Food Cost Indexes for Low-Income Households and the General Population, published by the [[Economic Research Service]], US Dept of Agriculture, TB-1872, p.7</ref><ref>Robert Cage; John Greenlees; Patrick Jackman. [http://www.bls.gov/cpi/super_paris.pdf Introducing the Chained Consumer Price Index]. For presentation at the Seventh Meeting of the International Working Group on Price Indices, May 2003</ref>
In a 1949 work,<ref>{{cite book|last1=Hyppölä|first1=J.|last2=Tunkelo|first2=A.|last3=Törnqvist|first3=L.|location=Helsinki|publisher=Statistics Finland|series=Tilastollisia tiedonantoja|title=Suomen väestöä, sen uusiutumista ja tulevaa kehitystä koskevia laskelmia|trans-title=Calculations concerning the population of Finland, its renewal and future development|language=Finnish|volume=38|year=1949}} As cited by {{harvtxt|Wiśniowski|Smith|Bijak|Bijak|2015}}</ref> he also made "the first serious attempt to describe population forecasting from a stochastic point of view",<ref>{{cite book|last1=Alho|first1=Juha M.|last2=Spencer|first2=Bruce D.|contribution=Statistical Propagation of Error in Forecasting|doi=10.1007/0-387-28392-7_9|pages=[https://archive.org/details/statisticaldemog00alho/page/n290 269]–295|publisher=Springer-Verlag|series=Springer Series in Statistics|title=Statistical Demography and Forecasting|year=2005|isbn=0-387-23530-2 |url=https://archive.org/details/statisticaldemog00alho|url-access=limited}}</ref> providing "seminal works" in [[Bayesian inference]] in [[demography]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Wiśniowski|first1=Arkadiusz|last2=Smith|first2=Peter W. F.|last3=Bijak|first3=Jakub|last4=Bijak|first4=James|last5=Forster|first5=Jonathan J.|date=May 2015|doi=10.1007/s13524-015-0389-y|issue=3|journal=Demography|pages=1035–1059|title=Bayesian Population Forecasting: Extending the Lee-Carter Method|volume=52|pmid=25962866|doi-access=free|url=https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/379875/1/Wisniowski_et_al_2015_Demography.pdf}}</ref>

As a professor at the University of Helsinki, his students included economist [[Timo Teräsvirta]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Jawadi|first=Fredj|date=June 2018|doi=10.1515/snde-2018-0021|issue=5|journal=Studies in Nonlinear Dynamics & Econometrics|title=An Interview with Timo Teräsvirta|volume=22|s2cid=158569911}}</ref> His student Vieno Rajaoja was the first Finnish woman to earn a doctorate in statistics, in 1958.<ref name=sk/>

==Recognition==
Törnqvist was elected member of the [[Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters]] in 1956,  fellow of the [[Econometric Society]] in 1951, and    member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 1956. He was decorated Commander of the [[Order of the Lion of Finland]] in 1961, and given honorary doctorates by the University of Helsinki in 1971 and by Åbo Akademi University in 1978.<ref name=sk/>

==Family==
In about 1981, Törnqvist bought a [[VIC-20]] and asked his daughter Anna's son, [[Linus Torvalds]], to help him program it. Törnqvist wrote out [[BASIC]] language programs, and grandson Linus, aged about eleven, typed them in. "He wanted me to share in the experience [and] get me interested in math," wrote Torvalds later.<ref>{{Cite book| last = Torvalds | first = Linus |author2=David Diamond  | title = [[Just for Fun (book)|Just For Fun: The Story of an Accidental Revolutionary]] | publisher  = HarperCollins | year = 2001 | location = New York City, US|isbn = 0-06-662072-4 }}, pp. 6-7.</ref> These were Linus's first programming experiences. Ten years later, Torvalds began to write the [[Linux kernel]].

Leo Törnqvist's brother was diplomat [[Erik Törnqvist]].<ref name=uf/> His son was the nuclear physicist {{ill|Nils Arthur Törnqvist|fi|Nils Törnqvist}} (1938–2018).<ref>{{cite news | author=Hoyer, Paul & Montonen, Claus & Roos, Matts | title=Kansainvälinen fyysikko | newspaper=Helsingin Sanomat | date=5 September 2018 | page= B 17 | url=http://www.hs.fi/muistot/art-2000005815327.html | trans-title=Orbituary for Nils Törnqvist | language=Finnish }}</ref>
